final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding lysine; alanine substitution removes Schiff-base formation, abolishing activity. AlphaMissense 0.987 strongly supports damaging effect.
C52 is the heme axial ligand in the N-terminal domain; its removal disrupts heme binding and CBS structural integrity. AlphaMissense 0.951 despite some alanine tolerance in MSA.
H65 sits in the heme-binding N-terminal region; its removal is plausibly destabilizing with AlphaMissense 0.845 (pathogenic). Slightly more uncertainty than the catalytic-site mutations.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are well-supported by strong pathogenicity scores and known catalytic/structural roles; additional tools would not alter the ranking.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the PLP (pyridoxal phosphate) Schiff-base cofactor-binding residue; its removal abolishes catalysis in CBS.
K119 is the PLP-binding catalytic lysine; removing it abolishes Schiff-base formation and is the most direct LOF mechanism.
K119 is the PLP-binding catalytic lysine; AlphaMissense 0.987 (strongly damaging) and low MSA tolerance for A support a decisive catalytic loss-of-function.
Even a conservative Lys-to-Arg change at the PLP-binding site disrupts cofactor linkage and strongly reduces CBS activity.
Conservative substitution at the PLP lysine still eliminates catalysis since Arg cannot form the internal aldimine.
Conservative K->R at the PLP lysine still scores pathogenic (0.777) but the charge retention may preserve partial function; demoted below the stronger alanine knockout.
Cys52 is a heme axial ligand in human CBS; mutating it disrupts heme binding and impairs enzyme activity/folding.
C52 is a heme-coordinating cysteine in CBS; disruption impairs heme binding and enzyme activity.

C52 is the heme-ligand cysteine; AlphaMissense 0.951 is strongly damaging. MSA shows some A tolerance (0.218), but the structural role of the heme ligand makes this a credible LOF variant; promoted to rank 2.
His65 is the second heme-coordinating ligand; loss of heme coordination destabilizes CBS and reduces activity.
H65 is implicated in heme ligation/catalytic-site geometry; alanine substitution likely disrupts activity.
AlphaMissense 0.845 (pathogenic); H65 sits near the heme/N-terminal region and removal is plausibly destabilizing; promoted to rank 3.
Gly307 lies in the catalytic core near the active-site loop; G307S is a well-known pathogenic loss-of-function CBS allele.
G307S is a well-known pathogenic CBS mutation causing loss of activity; confidence raised as a clinically validated LOF variant.
AlphaMissense 0.828 (pathogenic); known CBS-domain-adjacent region, but G307S is a common mild disease allele with residual activity, so kept as backup below top-3.
Ile278 is in the highly conserved catalytic domain; I278T is the most common pathogenic CBS mutation causing loss of function.
I278T is the most common pathogenic CBS allele causing homocystinuria via folding/activity loss; confidence raised given its established LOF phenotype.
AlphaMissense 0.159 (benign) directly contradicts the LOF goal; the most common CBS polymorphism is known to be functional, so rejected.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense 0.159 (benign) directly contradicts the LOF goal; the most common CBS polymorphism is known to be functional, so rejected.
